steps.say: Bladder pain syndrome is defined by time and sterility. Chronic pelvic pain with pressure or discomfort is centred on the bladder. Lower urinary tract symptoms are tracked alongside the pain daily. Six weeks of symptoms are required for the label. Infection is excluded by repeated cultures. Other pelvic diseases are excluded alongside by testing.
steps.tx: **Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome** (chronic bladder pain), **IC/BPS** (painful bladder condition), means **chronic pelvic pain** (persistent bladder centred ache), pressure, or discomfort with lower urinary tract symptoms beyond **6 weeks** (six weeks) and no infection. Exclude urinary infection, overactive bladder, and endometriosis before labelling. Grade pain and frequency with validated diaries, because severity guides therapy.

vis.alt: Diagram of acute bacterial cystitis showing ascending infection, umbrella cell invasion, and positive dipstick with leukocyte esterase and nitrite.
vis.caption: Bacterial cystitis is what sterile IC/BPS is not: exclude infection by repeated cultures. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Cystoscopy is used to separate ulcer from non ulcer disease. Hunner lesions are found in five to ten percent of patients. Circumscribed reddened mucosal patches are documented classically. Radiating capillaries are traced converging on each lesion. Hydrodistension is performed until the patches tear and bleed. Biopsy is added to exclude carcinoma in situ alongside.
steps.tx: **Hunner lesions** (bladder ulcers) appear in **5% to 10%** (five to ten in a hundred) as circumscribed erythematous mucosal patches with **radiating capillaries** (spoke vessels) that tear and bleed on **hydrodistension** (water stretch test). Fulfil the ulcer phenotype before destructive therapy. Always biopsy to exclude carcinoma in situ, because red patches deceive.

vis.alt: Bladder pain syndrome illustration with magnified wall showing a Hunner lesion, mucosal glomerulations, urothelial barrier defect, and mast cell infiltration.
vis.caption: Hunner lesion with glomerulations, barrier defect, and mast cells. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Hydrodistension is staged to show bleeds of two kinds routinely. Glomerulations are defined as petechial bleeds under the mucosa. They follow low pressure water stretching. These marks are shared with many bladder disorders. They are no longer accepted as mandatory signs. Diagnosis is based on pain with exclusion instead.
steps.tx: **Glomerulations** (petechial submucosal bleeds) after low pressure **hydrodistension** (water stretch) are non-specific and no longer mandatory or pathognomonic for diagnosis. Do not chase grade counts. Diagnose on chronic pain with sterile cultures and excluded mimics, because bleeding marks overlap widely across disorders.

steps.say: The bladder lining is sealed normally by its coating. A glycosaminoglycan layer is coated over the urothelium protectively. Disruption is followed by urinary potassium penetrating beneath. Sensory C fibres are fired by the leaking solutes. Mast cells are recruited and amplify pain. Barrier repair is targeted by instilled therapy.
steps.tx: **GAG layer** (protective bladder coating) of **glycosaminoglycan** (slime barrier) normally blocks urinary solutes, and its disruption lets potassium penetrate submucosa to fire sensory C-fibres and recruit **mast cells** (allergy pain cells). Treat the barrier as the therapeutic target. Intravesical replenishment calms the neural loop, because leaks drive neurogenic inflammation.

steps.say: One oral drug is licensed to target the disease itself. Pentosan polysulfate sodium is licensed for bladder pain. Elmiron one hundred mg is taken three times daily. Months of therapy are needed for benefit. Maculopathy screening is arranged before and during treatment. Retinal damage is monitored by eye specialists.
steps.tx: **Pentosan polysulfate sodium** (bladder coating drug), **Elmiron** (oral IC drug) **100 mg** (one hundred milligrams) three times daily, is the only oral disease specific therapy, needing months for benefit. Screen for **pigmentary maculopathy** (retinal spotting) at baseline and periodically on long therapy. Stop and refer promptly for visual symptoms, because retinal harm accrues silently.

steps.say: Nerve pain pathways are calmed at night. Amitriptyline is prescribed in low evening doses. Twenty five to seventy five mg is accepted as the usual range. Anticholinergic with antihistamine actions is added to settle urgency. Central pain modulation is expected with continued use. Morning drowsiness is warned about beforehand.
steps.tx: **Amitriptyline** (night-time nerve pain pill) **25 to 75 mg** (twenty five to seventy five milligrams) nightly eases symptoms through anticholinergic, antihistaminic, and **neuropathic pain modulation** (nerve calming) pathways. Start low and climb slowly against drowsiness. Review benefit with sedation burden each visit, because tolerance varies widely.

steps.say: Ulcer type disease is treated directly through the scope. Hunner lesions are fulgurated with cautery or laser. Triamcinolone is injected carefully beneath stubborn patches. Rapid profound remission is reported after treatment in most series. Repeat sessions are scheduled promptly for returning lesions. Bladder capacity is tracked carefully after each sitting.
steps.tx: **Hunner fulguration** (ulcer burning) by electrocautery or laser, or **triamcinolone injection** (steroid shot) beneath lesions, brings rapid profound remission in ulcer type disease. Repeat for returning ulcers and track capacity each time. Reserve cystectomy talk for end stage small fibrotic bladders, because fulguration saves most.

steps.say: Bladder bathing is used to treat the surface directly each session. DMSO with heparin is instilled through a catheter. Lidocaine is added routinely for immediate soothing. Hyaluronate is given to replenish the protective coat slowly. Weekly courses are repeated promptly for flares. Retention time is timed carefully with position changes.
steps.tx: **Intravesical therapy** (bladder bathing) with **DMSO** (anti-inflammatory solvent), **heparin instillation** (coating blood thinner), lidocaine, or hyaluronate restores the barrier and calms C-fibre inflammation. Instil weekly courses with timed retention and position rotation. Combine with oral therapy for stubborn cases, because layers of treatment stack benefit.
